p0_findings.summary: The legacy month-start detector depends on completion of the same UTC D1 bucket, including H1 availability after the 08:00 decision time. A 20-day return requires 21 closes, and an 08:00 H1 bar-open is not closed until 09:00; causal decision and entry semantics must be prospectively fixed or candidate 323 retired without replacement.
The implementation adds a UTC-date-plus-direction cross-instrument collapse and uses greedy overlap handling inconsistent with the frozen overlap-component wording.

The legacy-collapse bound of normally at most 48 applies only with common month-start dates. Under corrected per-instrument geometry, 192 is merely a coarse opportunity upper bound before warm-up, missing observations, absent signals, and episode overlap; it is not a realizable Count bound, and feasibility of the frozen minimum 120 remains unproven.
Candidate 321 is structurally close to rejected 319 and candidate 324 to rejected 314; without provenance evidence created before freeze, each affected candidate must be retired without replacement.
The anchored MTF report is structurally blocked and the legacy identity validator does not require structural QC pass.
The legacy runner has an incompletely pinned dynamic import chain, reads a prior outcome audit, and runs inside a full repository checkout.
The legacy workflow can skip cleanup after partial acquisition failure and records a cleanup claim before cleanup.

The 2017 and 2018 stages remain inside a noncanonical ACQUIRING transaction. Any future exception must verify 32 archives with exactly 54 regular members each, all 1664 source-member identities, safe paths, and rejection of duplicates and unknown members.
Existing H4/D1 grouping can accept 3-of-4 or 23-of-24 H1 inputs; exact independently generated timestamp-set equality is required.
Endpoint-only versus complete internal 96-hour H1 coverage is not frozen; any rule addition requires prospective amended preregistration, otherwise candidate 324 is retired without replacement.
